Paper: [Touvron et al. (2023), LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.13971).
This is an architecture reference for original LLaMA, with the broader experimental review still to be developed.

## Problem

The paper studies language models trained on large quantities of publicly available text, emphasizing useful performance at different inference budgets.
The architectural reading question is how text tokens pass through the decoder to become next-token scores. [Sections 1–2](https://arxiv.org/html/2302.13971v1#S2).

## Previous Attempts

LLaMA builds on the causal transformer and combines existing design choices: normalization before each sublayer, SwiGLU feedforward blocks, and rotary positional embeddings.
These mechanisms have distinct roles and should not be treated as one operation called attention. [Section 2.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2302.13971v1#S2.SS2).

## Architecture

Token IDs index learned embedding vectors.
Each decoder layer uses causal self-attention and a feedforward sublayer, with residual additions and RMSNorm before the sublayers.
Rotary position information modifies query and key representations used to compute attention.
The final hidden representation passes through normalization and a vocabulary projection to produce logits. [Section 2.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2302.13971v1#S2.SS2).

Training compares next-token logits with shifted text targets using cross-entropy.
Generation chooses successive tokens from the model's scores according to a decoding rule.
Softmax itself produces a probability distribution; it does not select the next token.
An implementation may fuse log-softmax into its training loss, so a diagram without a separate training softmax box does not mean normalization is absent.

## Diagram Caveats

The saved [architecture diagram](../../../images/notes/llama/imported-architecture.png) is retained as a study attachment with unrecorded authorship.
It includes useful labels for embeddings, rotary positions, residual paths, RMSNorm, SwiGLU, and a KV cache, but it is not an original-paper figure.

Its grouped-query-attention label should not be assigned to original LLaMA: the Llama 2 report identifies GQA as a later architectural change for larger models. [Llama 2, Section 2.2 and Table 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.09288#page=5).
Its fixed 32-layer stack also describes only a particular size; the original family includes different layer counts. [LLaMA, Table 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2302.13971v1#S2.T2).
The two nearby normalization labels around the attention input should not be read as evidence for two consecutive independent RMSNorm operations.

## Evidence and Limitations

The architecture attachment does not establish benchmark performance, training-data composition, or behavior of a particular checkpoint.
Those require a separate reading of the paper's experiments and the selected model configuration.
The original paper reports model-size-dependent evaluations in Section 3; this short note does not reproduce or assess them.
